functions.name: ggml_init
functions.signature: GGML_API struct ggml_context * ggml_init(struct ggml_init_params params);
functions.description: Create a new ggml_context (tensor arena) using the provided memory pool parameters. If params.mem_buffer is NULL, the arena is allocated internally; otherwise the caller-supplied buffer is used. Use this context to allocate tensors and graphs, and free it with ggml_free when done.
requirements: params.mem_size must be >= the total bytes needed for all tensors/graphs allocated in this context.
If params.mem_buffer is not NULL, it must point to at least params.mem_size bytes and remain valid for the lifetime of the context.
If params.no_alloc is true, tensor data buffers are not allocated; callers must not expect data pointers to be valid.
The returned ggml_context* must be released with ggml_free.

functions.name: ggml_reset
functions.description: Reset the allocation state in a ggml_context, effectively clearing arena allocations so new tensors can be allocated again within the same buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context returned by ggml_init.
All tensors referencing the old allocations become invalid after reset; callers must not use them.

functions.name: ggml_free
functions.description: Destroy a ggml_context and release its resources (and the internal buffer if it was internally allocated).
requirements: ctx must be a context previously returned by ggml_init.
After calling, all tensors/graphs from this context become invalid and must not be used.
If the context was created with a user-provided mem_buffer, only the ggml internal metadata is freed; the caller retains ownership of mem_buffer.

functions.signature: enum ggml_status ggml_backend_tensor_alloc(ggml_backend_buffer_t buffer, struct ggml_tensor * tensor, void * addr);

functions.name: ggml_backend_view_init
functions.description: Initializes a tensor view (non-owning slice/alias) backend metadata. Returns status.
requirements: tensor must be a valid ggml_tensor configured as a view
Caller must check returned ggml_status

functions.name: ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_from_ptr
functions.description: Wraps a host CPU memory pointer as a CPU backend buffer.
requirements: ptr must be a valid host pointer to at least size bytes
size must be > 0 and within addressable range
Returned buffer must be freed with ggml_backend_buffer_free

functions.name: ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type
functions.description: Returns the CPU backend buffer type, always available.

functions.name: ggml_backend_blas_init
functions.description: Initializes and returns a BLAS-based ggml backend instance. Use this to obtain a backend that executes ggml operations via a BLAS implementation. Typical usage: call once at startup to acquire a backend handle, then pass that handle to ggml APIs that accept a ggml_backend_t. Details about lifetime management and failure modes are not documented here; behavior if the underlying BLAS is unavailable is unknown.
requirements: Must be called before using the returned ggml_backend_t in other ggml operations.

functions.name: ggml_backend_is_blas
functions.description: Returns whether the given ggml backend handle corresponds to the BLAS backend. Useful for feature checks or conditional logic when multiple backends may be in use.
requirements: backend must be a valid ggml_backend_t obtained from ggml backend initialization (e.g., ggml_backend_blas_init or other ggml backend creators).
Behavior for a null or invalid backend is not documented; callers should pass only valid handles.

functions.name: ggml_backend_blas_set_n_threads
functions.description: Sets the number of threads used by the BLAS backend for internal work. The comment notes this controls threads used for conversion to float; for OpenBLAS and BLIS, it also sets the number of threads used for BLAS operations. Use to tune performance according to available CPU resources.
requirements: backend_blas must be a valid BLAS backend handle (e.g., returned by ggml_backend_blas_init).
n_threads specifies the desired thread count; exact valid range is not documented here and behavior for non-positive values is unspecified.
Effect on non-OpenBLAS/BLIS implementations is not specified beyond conversion-to-float threading.

functions.name: ggml_backend_blas_reg
functions.description: Returns the registry object for the BLAS backend. Typically used to register or query the BLAS backend with ggml’s backend registry mechanisms. Specific usage patterns depend on the surrounding ggml backend API.

Callers should handle the possibility of an unspecified/invalid return if the BLAS backend is not available (not documented).

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_reg
functions.description: Returns the registration handle for the CANN backend so it can be registered/queried within the ggml backend system. Typical usage is to obtain this handle and pass it to ggml backend registration or factory utilities.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should treat the returned ggml_backend_reg_t as an opaque handle suitable for ggml backend registration APIs.
Return value validity/lifetime management is governed by the ggml backend system; no ownership transfer is documented.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_init
functions.description: Initializes and returns a ggml backend instance bound to the specified CANN device. It validates the device index, allocates internal context, and creates a backend instance. Returns nullptr on failure.

Caller must check the return value for nullptr to handle initialization failure.
The returned ggml_backend_t is owned/managed per ggml backend lifecycle; destroy/release via the appropriate ggml backend API (details not provided here).

functions.name: ggml_backend_is_cann
functions.description: Determines whether the provided ggml backend instance is a CANN backend by comparing its GUID with the CANN backend’s GUID.
requirements: backend must be a valid ggml_backend_t obtained from ggml APIs; passing an invalid or uninitialized handle is undefined.
Returns true if backend is a CANN backend, false otherwise; caller should branch accordingly.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_buffer_type
functions.description: Returns the CANN device buffer type interface for the specified device. This is typically used to allocate buffers residing on the device. Access is implemented to be thread-safe.
requirements: device must be a valid device index in the range [0, ggml_backend_cann_get_device_count()).
On invalid device indices, the function may return nullptr; caller must check for nullptr before use.
Use the returned ggml_backend_buffer_type_t with ggml buffer allocation APIs compatible with this backend.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_get_device_count
functions.description: Returns the number of CANN devices detected/available according to ggml_cann_info().
requirements: No arguments required.
The return value is a non-negative count; callers should use it to bound device indices.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_host_buffer_type
functions.description: Returns a pinned host buffer type intended for use with the CPU backend to accelerate transfers between CPU and NPU.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should use the returned buffer type with the CPU backend for host allocations intended for faster CPU<->NPU copies.
Caller should check for nullptr return if allocation/initialization fails (not documented but common with buffer type getters).

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_get_device_description
functions.signature: GGML_BACKEND_API void ggml_backend_cann_get_device_description(int32_t device, char* description, size_t description_size);

If description_size is too small, truncation behavior and null-termination are not documented; callers should provide a sufficiently large buffer.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cann_get_device_memory
functions.signature: GGML_BACKEND_API void ggml_backend_cann_get_device_memory(int32_t device, size_t* free, size_t* total);
functions.description: Retrieves free and total memory sizes for the specified CANN device (ACL_HBM_MEM) and stores them in the provided locations.
requirements: device must be a valid device index in the range [0, ggml_backend_cann_get_device_count()).
free must be a non-null pointer to size_t where the free memory will be written.
total must be a non-null pointer to size_t where the total memory will be written.
Units are bytes unless otherwise specified by the implementation; not explicitly documented here.

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_init
functions.description: Initializes and returns a CUDA-based ggml backend instance bound to the specified device index. Typical usage is to query device count, choose a device, then initialize a backend for that device for running ggml computations on the GPU.
requirements: device must refer to a valid GPU index (typically 0 <= device < ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count())
Callers should use the returned ggml_backend_t only if non-null (unknown exact failure conditions)
The backend must be properly destroyed/cleaned up by the owning API (lifecycle management not shown here; unknown specifics)

functions.name: ggml_backend_is_cuda
functions.description: Returns true if the provided ggml backend instance is a CUDA backend, false otherwise. Useful to branch logic based on backend type.
requirements: backend must be a valid, initialized ggml_backend_t (unknown if NULL is allowed)
Does not modify the backend; can be called at any time after backend creation

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type
functions.description: Returns a buffer-type descriptor for allocating tensors/buffers on the specified CUDA device. Use this with ggml allocation APIs to place data directly on that GPU.
requirements: device must be a valid GPU index (typically 0 <= device < ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count())
Returned buffer type must be used with compatible backend APIs (general ggml constraint; details unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_split_buffer_type
functions.signature: ggml_backend_buffer_type_t ggml_backend_cuda_split_buffer_type(int main_device, const float * tensor_split);
functions.description: Returns a buffer-type descriptor that splits matrices by rows across multiple CUDA devices, anchored at main_device. Intended for model/tensor sharding across GPUs; tensor_split defines how rows are partitioned across devices.
requirements: main_device must be a valid GPU index (typically 0 <= main_device < ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count())
tensor_split must point to a valid array; its expected length/semantics are not documented here (unknown exact format and normalization)
Callers must ensure the split configuration matches available devices; behavior for mismatches is unspecified (unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_host_buffer_type
functions.description: Returns a buffer-type descriptor for pinned (page-locked) host memory to speed up CPU–GPU transfers when used with the CPU backend.
requirements: No arguments; returned buffer type should be used where pinned host memory is required by ggml APIs (exact pairing rules unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count
functions.description: Returns the number of CUDA-capable devices available to the runtime (up to an internal maximum). Use this to enumerate/select devices.
requirements: No arguments; caller should handle zero or negative values as failure or no-device cases (exact failure semantics unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_description
functions.signature: void ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_description(int device, char * description, size_t description_size);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable description of the specified CUDA device into the provided buffer. Intended for UI/logging to identify GPUs.

description must be a valid, writable buffer

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_memory
functions.signature: void ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_memory(int device, size_t * free, size_t * total);
functions.description: Retrieves the current free and total memory, in bytes, for the specified CUDA device. Writes results to the provided output pointers.
requirements: device must be a valid GPU index (typically 0 <= device < ggml_backend_cuda_get_device_count())
free must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving free memory
total must be a non-null pointer to size_t for receiving total memory
Function does not return a status; caller must assume outputs are valid if pointers are valid (error signaling behavior unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_register_host_buffer
functions.description: Registers a host memory region for pinned/page-locked access to accelerate transfers between CPU and GPU. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, non-null host pointer to memory that the process owns
size must be > 0 and must not exceed the allocated region size for buffer
Buffer should be unregistered with ggml_backend_cuda_unregister_host_buffer when no longer needed; double registration/unregistration behaviors are unspecified (unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_unregister_host_buffer
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered pinned host memory region. After this call, the memory is no longer pinned for accelerated transfers.
requirements: buffer must be the same pointer previously passed to ggml_backend_cuda_register_host_buffer
Passing an unregistered or null pointer has unspecified behavior (unknown)

functions.name: ggml_backend_cuda_reg
functions.description: Returns the CUDA backend registration object used to integrate the CUDA backend into the ggml backend registry system. Typically used for global registration or querying backend capabilities.
requirements: No arguments; returned registration object should be used with ggml’s backend registry APIs (exact usage patterns unknown)

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_init
functions.signature: GGML_API ggml_opt_dataset_t ggml_opt_dataset_init(enum ggml_type type_data, enum ggml_type type_label, int64_t ne_datapoint, int64_t ne_label, int64_t ndata, int64_t ndata_shard);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a dataset handle with internal GGML tensors for data and labels, using the provided element types and shapes. Intended as the dataset container used by the optimizer/training utilities.
requirements: type_data and type_label must be valid ggml_type values.
ne_datapoint is the number of elements per datapoint; ne_label is the number of elements per label.
ndata is the total number of datapoints/labels in the dataset.
ndata_shard is the shard size (granularity for shuffling/copying).
The resulting internal tensors have shapes: data -> [ne_datapoint, ndata], labels -> [ne_label, ndata].
Caller must later free the dataset via ggml_opt_dataset_free.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_free
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a dataset created by ggml_opt_dataset_init.
requirements: dataset must be a handle previously returned by ggml_opt_dataset_init or NULL.
After this call, the dataset handle must not be used.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_ndata
functions.description: Returns the number of datapoints stored in the dataset.
requirements: dataset must be a valid dataset handle.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_data
functions.description: Returns the internal data tensor for the dataset. Shape is [ne_datapoint, ndata].
requirements: dataset must be a valid dataset handle.
Returned tensor is owned by the dataset; do not free it independently.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_labels
functions.description: Returns the internal labels tensor for the dataset. Shape is [ne_label, ndata].
requirements: dataset must be a valid dataset handle.
Returned tensor is owned by the dataset; do not free it independently.
Labels may be unused depending on loss type.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_shuffle
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_dataset_shuffle(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, int64_t idata);
functions.description: Shuffles the dataset in-place using the RNG from opt_ctx. Shuffles the first idata datapoints, or all datapoints if idata is negative.
requirements: opt_ctx must be a valid optimization context with RNG.
dataset must be a valid dataset handle.
If idata is negative, all datapoints are shuffled; otherwise the first idata datapoints are shuffled.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_get_batch
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_dataset_get_batch(ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, struct ggml_tensor * data_batch, struct ggml_tensor * labels_batch, int64_t ibatch);
functions.description: Copies a batch at logical position ibatch from the dataset into the provided data_batch and labels_batch tensors.
requirements: dataset must be valid and populated.
data_batch must be a tensor with shape [ne_datapoint, ndata_batch].
labels_batch must be a tensor with shape [ne_label, ndata_batch].
ibatch selects which batch to copy; mapping to indices depends on dataset/shard settings.
Shapes must match the dataset’s ne_datapoint and ne_label and the intended batch size.

functions.name: ggml_opt_dataset_get_batch_host
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_dataset_get_batch_host(ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, void * data_batch, size_t nb_data_batch, void * labels_batch, int64_t ibatch);
functions.description: Copies a batch at position ibatch from the dataset into host memory buffers for data and labels.
requirements: dataset must be valid and populated.
data_batch must point to a writable host buffer large enough to hold the batch data; nb_data_batch specifies its byte size.
labels_batch must point to a writable host buffer large enough for the labels batch.
ibatch selects which batch to copy; mapping to indices depends on dataset/shard settings.
Buffer sizes must be consistent with element types and batch shape [ne_datapoint, ndata_batch] and [ne_label, ndata_batch].

functions.name: ggml_opt_get_default_optimizer_params
functions.description: Returns a struct of hard-coded default optimizer parameters. The userdata pointer is ignored.
requirements: Caller should ignore userdata; it is not used.
Use when constant default hyperparameters are desired.

functions.name: ggml_opt_get_constant_optimizer_params
functions.description: Interprets userdata as a pointer to ggml_opt_optimizer_params and returns the dereferenced parameters, enabling caller-supplied fixed hyperparameters.
requirements: userdata must point to a valid ggml_opt_optimizer_params struct.
The pointed struct must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_default_params
functions.signature: GGML_API struct ggml_opt_params ggml_opt_default_params(ggml_backend_sched_t backend_sched, enum ggml_opt_loss_type loss_type);
functions.description: Constructs an optimization parameter set with sensible defaults where possible, requiring the backend scheduler and loss type as inputs.
requirements: backend_sched must be a valid ggml backend scheduler.
loss_type must be a valid ggml_opt_loss_type.
Caller may customize the returned struct before initializing a context.

functions.name: ggml_opt_init
functions.description: Initializes and returns an optimization context based on the supplied parameters (backend, graphs, loss, optimizer, etc.).
requirements: params must be initialized, typically via ggml_opt_default_params and then customized.
If using static graphs, params.ctx_compute, params.inputs, and params.outputs should be set as described by comments.
Caller must free the returned context with ggml_opt_free.

functions.name: ggml_opt_free
functions.description: Frees resources held by an optimization context created with ggml_opt_init.
requirements: opt_ctx must be a valid context or NULL.
Do not use opt_ctx after freeing.

functions.name: ggml_opt_reset
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_reset(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, bool optimizer);
functions.description: Resets training state: zeroes gradients, initializes loss, and optionally resets optimizer state.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If optimizer is true, optimizer internal state (e.g., moments) is reset; otherwise only gradients/loss are reset.

functions.name: ggml_opt_static_graphs
functions.description: Returns whether the compute graphs are allocated statically within the optimization context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.

functions.name: ggml_opt_inputs
functions.description: Returns the forward graph input tensor associated with the optimization context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_outputs
functions.description: Returns the forward graph output tensor associated with the optimization context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_labels
functions.description: Returns the labels tensor used to compare outputs against within the context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_loss
functions.description: Returns the scalar loss tensor in the optimization context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_pred
functions.description: Returns the predictions tensor derived from outputs in the context.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_ncorrect
functions.description: Returns a tensor containing the number of correct predictions (matches between outputs and labels).
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
If not using static graphs, the returned pointer becomes invalid after the next ggml_opt_alloc call.

functions.name: ggml_opt_grad_acc

functions.description: Returns the gradient accumulator tensor corresponding to a node from the forward graph.
requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
node must be a tensor that is part of the forward graph built/managed by this context.

functions.name: ggml_opt_context_optimizer_type
functions.description: Returns the optimizer type associated with the given optimization context.
requirements: Argument must be a valid optimization context.

functions.name: ggml_opt_optimizer_name
functions.description: Returns a string name for a given optimizer type.
requirements: Argument must be a valid ggml_opt_optimizer_type value.
Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not free.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an optimization-result accumulator object.
requirements: Caller must free the result with ggml_opt_result_free when done.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_free
functions.description: Frees a result object created by ggml_opt_result_init.
requirements: result must be a valid result handle or NULL.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_reset
functions.description: Resets/clears the accumulated values in a result object.
requirements: result must be valid.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_ndata
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_result_ndata(ggml_opt_result_t result, int64_t * ndata);

ndata must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for 1 int64_t.

functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_result_loss(ggml_opt_result_t result, double * loss, double * unc);

loss must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for 1 double.
unc may be NULL to ignore uncertainty; if not NULL, it must be writable.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_pred
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_result_pred(ggml_opt_result_t result, int32_t * pred);
functions.description: Writes per-datapoint predictions into pred; writes ndata values.

pred must point to a writable buffer large enough for ndata int32_t values.
Caller should obtain ndata via ggml_opt_result_ndata to size the buffer.

functions.name: ggml_opt_result_accuracy
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_result_accuracy(ggml_opt_result_t result, double * accuracy, double * unc);
functions.description: Writes the aggregate accuracy into accuracy (one value). If unc is non-NULL, writes the accuracy uncertainty there.
requirements: result must be valid.
accuracy must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory for 1 double.
unc may be NULL to ignore uncertainty; if not NULL, it must be writable.

functions.name: ggml_opt_prepare_alloc
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_prepare_alloc(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, struct ggml_context * ctx_compute, struct ggml_cgraph * gf, struct ggml_tensor * inputs, struct ggml_tensor * outputs);
functions.description: If not using static graphs, prepares the context for allocation by providing the compute context, graph, inputs, and outputs prior to ggml_opt_alloc.

functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_alloc(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, bool backward);

requirements: opt_ctx must be valid.
Must be invoked exactly once prior to a corresponding ggml_opt_eval.
If backward is true, the graph will support a backward pass; otherwise forward-only.

functions.name: ggml_opt_eval
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_eval(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, ggml_opt_result_t result);

requirements: opt_ctx must be valid and have been prepared/allocated via ggml_opt_alloc.
result may be NULL to skip accumulation; if non-NULL it must be a valid result handle.

functions.name: ggml_opt_epoch
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_epoch(ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, ggml_opt_result_t result_train, ggml_opt_result_t result_eval, int64_t idata_split, ggml_opt_epoch_callback callback_train, ggml_opt_epoch_callback callback_eval);

dataset must be a valid dataset with data (and labels if required by loss).
result_train and result_eval may be NULL to ignore accumulation for that phase; otherwise must be valid result handles.
idata_split specifies the index separating training and evaluation subsets.
callback_train and callback_eval may be NULL to disable callbacks, or valid function pointers matching ggml_opt_epoch_callback.

functions.name: ggml_opt_epoch_callback_progress_bar
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_epoch_callback_progress_bar(bool train, ggml_opt_context_t opt_ctx, ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, ggml_opt_result_t result, int64_t ibatch, int64_t ibatch_max, int64_t t_start_us);
functions.description: A ready-to-use callback that prints a progress bar to stderr for training or evaluation within ggml_opt_epoch.
requirements: Arguments must match the ggml_opt_epoch_callback signature when used as a callback.
result may be NULL per epoch caller’s usage.
ibatch and ibatch_max should reflect current and total batches.
t_start_us is the epoch subsection start time in microseconds.

functions.name: ggml_opt_fit
functions.signature: GGML_API void ggml_opt_fit(ggml_backend_sched_t backend_sched, struct ggml_context * ctx_compute, struct ggml_tensor * inputs, struct ggml_tensor * outputs, ggml_opt_dataset_t dataset, enum ggml_opt_loss_type loss_type, enum ggml_opt_optimizer_type optimizer, ggml_opt_get_optimizer_params get_opt_pars, int64_t nepoch, int64_t nbatch_logical, float val_split, bool silent);
functions.description: High-level training driver that fits the model defined by inputs/outputs to the dataset using the specified loss and optimizer. Iterates for nepoch epochs, performs optimizer steps at the given logical batch size, optionally splits data for validation, and uses a hyperparameter callback.
requirements: backend_sched must be a valid backend scheduler.
ctx_compute must be a GGML context for temporarily allocated tensors to compute outputs (built with no_alloc == true per usage notes).
inputs must be a tensor with shape [ne_datapoint, ndata_batch].
outputs must be a tensor; if labels are used, it must have shape [ne_label, ndata_batch].
dataset must be valid and populated (and include labels when required by the selected loss_type).
loss_type and optimizer must be valid enum values.
get_opt_pars is a callback to obtain optimizer params; its userdata is a pointer to the epoch (int64_t) as documented.

import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for "arbitrary binary data" that will be fed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR across
# multiple stubs. We want to produce valid, interesting bytes for:
# - float rows (fp32 source for fp16/bf16 conversions): include NaNs, infinities,
#   subnormals, small/large magnitudes, alternating signs, special patterns.
# - fp16/bf16 storage rows: 16-bit payload patterns including zeros, subnormals,
#   infinities, NaNs, alternating bit patterns.
# - GUIDs: 16-byte sequences with structure variants (all-zero, all-FF, UUID-like).
# - Backend tensor set payloads: arbitrary sized blobs up to ~1KB, include repeated
#   patterns, increasing counters, random bytes.
#
# The fuzzer harness calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times per invocation. We cannot
# control which call receives which of our sequences, but we can concatenate a bag
# of varied-length segments separated by small random paddings, so that each call
# slices from our corpus and still gets meaningful content.
#
# Constraints:
# - Return <= 4096 bytes
# - Seeded randomness
# - Self-contained, no I/O

# Helpers to build interesting floats and 16-bit payloads

def _f32_bits(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _f32(val: float) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<f', val)

def _u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def _float_special_corpus():
    # Include canonical specials and a range of magnitudes
    vals = [
        0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 0.5, -0.5, 2.0, -2.0,
        1e-38, -1e-38, 1e-45, -1e-45,  # subnormal/near-underflow
        3.4e38, -3.4e38,               # near max finite
        float('inf'), float('-inf')
    ]
    # NaN payloads: quiet/signaling variants
    nan_bits = [0x7FC00000, 0x7FA00001, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x7F800001, 0xFFC00000, 0x7FC01234]
    data = bytearray()
    for v in vals:
        data += _f32(v)
    for b in nan_bits:
        data += _f32_bits(b)
    # Alternating signs with incremental magnitudes
    for i in range(1, 33):
        v = (-1.0 if i % 2 else 1.0) * (2.0 ** (i % 16)) / (i)
        data += _f32(v)
    return bytes(data)


def _fp16_like_corpus():
    # 16-bit payloads for fp16 storage: zeros, subnormals, normals, inf, NaN, patterns
    patterns = [
        0x0000, 0x8000,        # +0, -0
        0x3C00, 0xBC00,        # +1.0, -1.0
        0x7C00, 0xFC00,        # +inf, -inf
        0x7E00, 0xFE00,        # qNaN payloads
        0x0001, 0x8001,        # smallest subnormal
        0x03FF, 0x83FF,        # largest subnormal
        0x7BFF, 0xFBFF,        # max finite
        0x3555, 0xB555,        # 1/3 approx patterns
        0xAAAA, 0x5555,        # alternating bits
        0x0123, 0x89AB, 0xCDEF
    ]
    data = bytearray()
    for p in patterns:
        data += _u16(p)
    # short sequences mixing signs
    for i in range(1, 33):
        x = (0x0400 + i) | (0x8000 if i % 2 else 0)
        data += _u16(x)
    return bytes(data)


def _bf16_like_corpus():
    # bfloat16 payloads are just the high 16 bits of IEEE754 float32; include similar set
    patterns = [
        0x0000, 0x8000,        # +0, -0
        0x3F80, 0xBF80,        # +1.0, -1.0
        0x7F80, 0xFF80,        # +inf, -inf
        0x7FC0, 0xFFC0,        # qNaN typical
        0x0080, 0x8080,        # small subnormals in bf16 domain
        0x7F7F, 0xFF7F,        # near max finite
        0x5555, 0xAAAA, 0x1234, 0xC001
    ]
    data = bytearray()
    for p in patterns:
        data += _u16(p)
    for i in range(1, 33):
        x = ((0x3F00 + i) & 0x7FFF) | (0x8000 if i % 3 == 0 else 0)
        data += _u16(x)
    return bytes(data)


def _guid_corpus(rng: random.Random):
    corpus = []
    # All zeros and all FF
    corpus.append(bytes(16))
    corpus.append(b"\xFF" * 16)
    # Incrementing and decrementing sequences
    corpus.append(bytes([i % 256 for i in range(16)]))
    corpus.append(bytes([(255 - i) % 256 for i in range(16)]))
    # UUID-like: version 4 random
    for _ in range(2):
        b = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
        b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0F) | 0x40  # version 4
        b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80  # variant
        corpus.append(bytes(b))
    # Some repeated 16-byte blocks with small edits
    base = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    corpus.append(bytes(base))
    for i in range(3):
        bb = bytearray(base)
        bb[i] ^= 0xFF
        corpus.append(bytes(bb))
    return b"".join(corpus)


def _blob_payloads(rng: random.Random):
    # Various sizes up to ~1024 bytes to satisfy tensor set calls
    bufs = []
    # Repeated pattern bytes
    for pat in [b"\x00", b"\xFF", b"A", b"\x7F", b"\x80"]:
        bufs.append(pat * rng.randint(8, 128))
    # Increasing counters
    inc = bytes([i % 256 for i in range(rng.randint(32, 256))])
    bufs.append(inc)
    # Random block
    n = rng.randint(64, 512)
    bufs.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n)))
    # Mixed small chunks concatenated
    chunks = []
    for _ in range(10):
        m = rng.randint(4, 32)
        chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(m)))
    bufs.append(b"".join(chunks))
    return b"".join(bufs)


def _pad(rng: random.Random, max_len=16):
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, max_len)))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build themed segments that different FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can consume:
    segments = []

    # Float32 heavy segment
    segments.append(_float_special_corpus())
    segments.append(_pad(rng))

    # FP16 storage patterns
    segments.append(_fp16_like_corpus())
    segments.append(_pad(rng))

    # BF16 storage patterns
    segments.append(_bf16_like_corpus())
    segments.append(_pad(rng))

    # GUIDs
    segments.append(_guid_corpus(rng))
    segments.append(_pad(rng))

    # Payload blobs for backend tensor_set(_async)
    segments.append(_blob_payloads(rng))

    # Shuffle some smaller extra snippets to increase variety across calls
    extras = []
    for _ in range(8):
        choice = rng.choice(['f32', 'fp16', 'bf16', 'rand', 'zeros'])
        if choice == 'f32':
            # a short run of random float32s
            cnt = rng.randint(4, 32)
            data = bytearray()
            for _ in range(cnt):
                # random bit-pattern to cover NaNs too
                data += _f32_bits(rng.getrandbits(32))
            extras.append(bytes(data))
        elif choice == 'fp16':
            cnt = rng.randint(8, 64)
            data = bytearray()
            for i in range(cnt):
                # biased towards interesting exponents
                if i % 8 == 0:
                    v = rng.choice([0x7C00, 0xFC00, 0x7E00, 0xFE00, 0x0000, 0x8000])
                else:
                    v = rng.getrandbits(16)
                data += _u16(v)
            extras.append(bytes(data))
        elif choice == 'bf16':
            cnt = rng.randint(8, 64)
            data = bytearray()
            for i in range(cnt):
                if i % 8 == 0:
                    v = rng.choice([0x7F80, 0xFF80, 0x7FC0, 0xFFC0, 0x0000, 0x8000])
                else:
                    v = rng.getrandbits(16)
                data += _u16(v)
            extras.append(bytes(data))
        elif choice == 'rand':
            m = rng.randint(16, 128)
            extras.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(m)))
        else:
            m = rng.randint(16, 128)
            extras.append(b"\x00" * m)

    rng.shuffle(extras)
    segments.extend(extras)

    # Concatenate with small random paddings in between to reduce accidental merging
    out = bytearray()
    for seg in segments:
        out += seg
        out += _pad(rng, max_len=8)

    # Trim to limit
    limit = 4096
    if len(out) > limit:
        # Keep head and tail to preserve variety for early and later consumers
        head_keep = int(limit * 0.6)
        tail_keep = limit - head_keep
        out = bytearray(out[:head_keep] + out[-tail_keep:])

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
import string

def _rand_utf8_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a short, valid UTF-8 filename, avoid directory traversal and NUL
    # Include a mix of ascii, some unicode, and common extensions
    base_choices = [
        "data", "model", "weights", "tensor", "gguf", "config", "tmp", "notes",
        "输入", "данные", "データ", "δοκιμή", "prüf", "tést",
    ]
    ext_choices = ["", ".bin", ".gguf", ".txt", ".dat", ".log"]

    base = rng.choice(base_choices)
    # Add some random safe chars
    safe_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
    tail = ''.join(rng.choice(safe_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
    ext = rng.choice(ext_choices)
    name = base + tail + ext
    # Randomly choose a simple subdir prefix to vary directories
    subdirs = ["", "sub", "dir", "á", "数据"]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        d = rng.choice(subdirs)
        if d:
            return os.path.join(d, name)
    return name


def _rand_file_contents(rng: random.Random, max_size: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    # Generate interesting binary contents with mixed patterns
    parts = []
    # header-like magic options
    magics = [b"GGUF", b"\x7fELF", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", b"BM", b"\xff\xd8\xff", b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice(magics))
    # random floats/ints
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
        parts.append(struct.pack('<I', rng.getrandbits(32)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(struct.pack('<f', rng.uniform(-1e3, 1e3)))
    # some text chunk
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        text = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 64)))
        parts.append(text.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    # random bytes tail
    tail_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, max_size - sum(len(p) for p in parts)))
    parts.append(rng.randbytes(tail_len))
    data = b''.join(parts)
    return data[:max_size]


def _pack_filename_and_mode(filename: str, mode: str) -> bytes:
    # FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME reads a filename separately; our single buffer should include
    # a filename string and a mode selector. We serialize as:
    # [u32 name_len][name_bytes][u32 mode_index]
    name_b = filename.encode('utf-8')
    modes = [b"rb", b"r", b"wb", b"w", b"rb+", b"ab", b"a"]
    try:
        m_idx = modes.index(mode.encode('ascii'))
    except ValueError:
        m_idx = 0
    return struct.pack('<I', len(name_b)) + name_b + struct.pack('<I', m_idx)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a pair: an existing file path for reading tests and a new file path for writing tests
    # We will include one filename that likely exists within the fuzzer sandbox by providing
    # inline file content and name so the harness can create the file. Since we cannot do I/O here,
    # we encode both the intended filename and its desired contents so the fuzzer harness can materialize it.

    # Build two filenames
    fname_read = _rand_utf8_filename(rng)
    fname_write = _rand_utf8_filename(rng)

    # Ensure they are distinct
    if fname_write == fname_read:
        fname_write += "_w"

    # Select modes exercising read and write paths
    read_modes = ["rb", "r", "rb+"]
    write_modes = ["wb", "w", "ab", "a", "rb+"]
    mode_read = rng.choice(read_modes)
    mode_write = rng.choice(write_modes)

    # Generate contents for the readable file, and optional initial contents for the write target when using append/update
    read_contents = _rand_file_contents(rng, max_size=1024)
    write_seed_contents = b""
    if mode_write in ("ab", "a", "rb+") and rng.random() < 0.7:
        write_seed_contents = _rand_file_contents(rng, max_size=256)

    # We must return a single bytes buffer. Layout:
    # [u32 count_files]
    # For each file:
    #   [u32 name_len][name][u32 content_len][content]
    # Then two operations for the stubs parameters:
    #   For ggml_fopen: [u32 name_len][name][u32 mode_index]
    #   For gguf_write_to_file: [u32 name_len][name][u32 only_meta_flag]
    # This allows the fuzzer harness (or a wrapper) to create files before invoking stubs.

    out = bytearray()

    # Files to create: readable file and maybe seed for writable
    files = [(fname_read, read_contents)]
    if write_seed_contents:
        files.append((fname_write, write_seed_contents))

    out += struct.pack('<I', len(files))
    for name, content in files:
        nb = name.encode('utf-8')
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(nb)) + nb
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(content)) + content

    # ggml_fopen params
    out += _pack_filename_and_mode(fname_read, mode_read)

    # gguf_write_to_file params: filename and only_meta flag
    only_meta = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
    nbw = fname_write.encode('utf-8')
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(nbw)) + nbw + struct.pack('<I', only_meta)

    # Cap to 4096 bytes
    return bytes(out[:4096])

import random
import struct
import sys
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: UTF-8 string (null-terminated when used by C APIs)
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and sometimes integers; our single buffer
# should prioritize supplying interesting valid UTF-8 strings since all stubs
# use strings for names/keys/values. The engine will split the buffer for multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls, so we generate a sequence of well-formed UTF-8 strings
# separated by NULs. This ensures c_str() reads valid C strings and the library
# deep-copies them as needed.
#
# We generate several strings to cover:
# - ASCII simple identifiers (for ggml tensor names, gguf keys)
# - Keys with dots and slashes (e.g., namespace-like keys used by gguf)
# - Empty string and very short strings
# - Long strings up to a safe cap (<= 60 for ggml names, but fuzzer truncates if longer)
# - Unicode strings across multiple planes (Latin-1 supplement, Cyrillic, CJK, emoji)
# - Strings with spaces and punctuation
# - Format parts safe for printf (no stray % characters) for ggml_format_name
#
# The buffer size is limited to <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.:/"  # useful in keys/names
PRINT_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

# Some curated Unicode samples to ensure coverage
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "naïve",                 # Latin-1
    "mañana",               # Latin-1
    "русский",              # Cyrillic
    "日本語テキスト",          # CJK + Katakana
    "한국어",                 # Hangul
    "العربية",               # Arabic (RTL but fine as bytes)
    "हिन्दी",                # Devanagari
    "🙂🙃🚀✨",                # Emoji
    "ẽ̃ ̃ combining",        # combining marks
]

# Utility to build a random ASCII identifier-like key
def rand_key(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

# Utility to build a random printable ASCII phrase (no NUL, no % for printf safety)
def rand_phrase(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # avoid '%' to keep printf-style formatting safe for "%s-%u"
    allowed = PRINT_ASCII.replace('%', '')
    return ''.join(rng.choice(allowed) for _ in range(n))

# Build a mixed UTF-8 string with a chance to include curated samples
def rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # 50% use curated sample, maybe extended with ascii
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        # Optionally pad with some ascii to vary length
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, max(0, max_len - len(base)))))
        s = base + extra
        if len(s) < min_len:
            s += rand_phrase(rng, min_len - len(s), min_len - len(s))
        return s[:max_len]
    else:
        # Build from a mix of ranges
        target = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
        out = []
        while len(''.join(out)) < target:
            p = rng.random()
            if p < 0.6:
                out.append(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII))
            elif p < 0.8:
                out.append(rng.choice("àáâãäåçèéêëìíîïñòóôõöùúûüýÿøÞðşğıłżźšž"))
            elif p < 0.95:
                out.append(rng.choice("абвгдезийклмнопрстуфхцчшщыэюя"))
            else:
                out.append(rng.choice(["日", "本", "語", "テ", "キ", "ス", "ト", "🙂", "🚀", "✨"]))
        return ''.join(out)[:max_len]

# Assemble a sequence of NUL-terminated strings into bytes
def pack_cstrings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b"\x00"
        if total + len(b) > 4096:
            break
        parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)
    return b''.join(parts)

# Generate a set of interesting keys for gguf
def build_keys(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    keys = []
    # Known fixed keys used by stubs to ensure presence
    keys.append("fuzz.val.str")
    keys.append("fuzz.arr.str")
    keys.append("fuzz.set.str")
    keys.append("fuzz.set.arr.str")
    # Namespace-like random keys
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        ns = rand_key(rng, 3, 8)
        sub = rand_key(rng, 3, 10)
        keys.append(f"{ns}.{sub}")
    return keys

# Generate a set of names suitable for ggml_set_name / ggml_get_tensor
def build_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    # include empty and short names; the stubs truncate to 60 if longer
    names.append("")
    names.append("a")
    names.append("tensor")
    names.append("name_with.dots-and/slashes")
    names.append(rand_key(rng, 8, 20))
    names.append(rand_key(rng, 30, 65))  # longer than 60 to exercise truncation in stub
    # include unicode names
    names.append(rand_utf8(rng, 3, 40))
    return names

# Generate parts for ggml_format_name (used with "%s-%u")
# Must not contain '%', and reasonable length <= 40; we ensure that.
def build_format_parts(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts = []
    parts.append("part")
    parts.append(rand_phrase(rng, 1, 10))
    parts.append(rand_phrase(rng, 15, 35))
    parts.append(rand_phrase(rng, 35, 40))
    return parts

# Strings for gguf values and arrays
def build_values(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    vals = []
    # simple ascii values
    vals.append(rand_phrase(rng, 0, 12))
    vals.append(rand_phrase(rng, 1, 24))
    # unicode-rich values
    vals.append(rand_utf8(rng, 1, 40))
    vals.append(rand_utf8(rng, 1, 60))
    return vals

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose a pool of strings in an order that helps the stubs:
    strings: List[str] = []

    # 1) Names for ggml tensors
    strings += build_names(rng)

    # 2) Format parts for ggml_format_name
    strings += build_format_parts(rng)

    # 3) Known gguf keys and extra random keys
    strings += build_keys(rng)

    # 4) Values for gguf strings and arrays
    strings += build_values(rng)

    # 5) Additional random utf-8 to increase diversity
    extra_count = rng.randint(3, 7)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        strings.append(rand_utf8(rng, 0, 50))

    # Ensure uniqueness and keep order for earlier duplicates
    seen = set()
    uniq_strings = []
    for s in strings:
        if s not in seen:
            uniq_strings.append(s)
            seen.add(s)

    buf = pack_cstrings(uniq_strings)

    # Guarantee at least one NUL byte if empty
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"

    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: ASCII identifier (C-string) used as a procedure/symbol name.
# This generator returns bytes intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# and ultimately passed as const char* to ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, null-terminated-friendly strings (Python bytes without embedded NUL; fuzzer will handle C-string view)
# - Cover typical symbol patterns and edge cases (empty, long, mixed case, digits/underscores, namespaces, vendor prefixes,
#   versioned names, dashes/periods/at-suffixes often seen in dynamic symbol names, and unusual but printable chars).
# - Limit size <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_LEN = 512  # keep well under 4096

_common_prefixes = [
    "ggml_", "gguf_", "ggml_backend_", "ggml_backend_cuda_", "ggml_backend_rpc_",
    "ggml_backend_vk_", "ggml_backend_webgpu_", "ggml_backend_blas_", "ggml_opt_",
]

_common_symbols = [
    # Very common query targets
    "ggml_init", "ggml_free", "ggml_new_graph", "ggml_new_graph_custom", "ggml_graph_dup",
    "ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address", "ggml_backend_free", "ggml_backend_buffer_free",
    "ggml_backend_cuda_init", "ggml_backend_cuda_reg", "ggml_backend_rpc_init", "ggml_backend_rpc_reg",
    "ggml_backend_vk_init", "ggml_backend_webgpu_init", "ggml_backend_webgpu_reg",

# Some library-like suffix decorations sometimes used by linkers or toolchains
_suffixes = ["", "@", "@@", "@GLIBC_2.17", "@LLVM", "@@LIBGGML_1", "@v1", "@v2", "@CUDART"]

# Allowed characters for identifiers and extended symbol-like names
_ident_start = string.ascii_letters + "_"
_ident_body = _ident_start + string.digits
_extra_sym_chars = "._:$-"  # occasionally seen in mangled or toolchain-specific names


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 40) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    s = [rng.choice(_ident_start)]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        # mix identifier body and a few extra safe symbol chars
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            s.append(rng.choice(_extra_sym_chars))
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(_ident_body))
    return "".join(s)


def _version_tag(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # common version tag patterns
    choices = [
        "", "_v1", "_v2", "_v3", "_x64", "_x86", "_avx2", "_avx512", "_neon", "_cuda", "_cpu",
        "_opt", "_fast", "_debug", "_release"
    ]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _namespace(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # occasionally namespaced like ggml::backend::name (C++-style) or module.name
    styles = ["", "::", ":", "."]
    ns_depth = rng.choices([0, 1, 2, 3], weights=[0.6, 0.25, 0.1, 0.05])[0]
    if ns_depth == 0:
        return ""
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(ns_depth):
        parts.append(_rand_ident(rng, 2, 10))
    sep = rng.choice(styles)
    return sep.join(parts) + sep


def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[float]) -> str:
    return rng.choices(items, weights=weights, k=1)[0]


def _build_symbol(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix several construction strategies
    strategies = [
        "common",          # direct from known list
        "prefixed",        # prefix + ident
        "namespaced",      # namespace + ident
        "compound",        # prefix + ident + version
        "mangled_like",    # add dots/at suffixes
        "bare_ident",      # just an identifier
        "edge_short",      # very short
        "edge_long",       # long but still reasonable
        "camel_case",      # camelCase style
    ]
    strat = rng.choice(strategies)

    if strat == "common" and _common_symbols:
        base = rng.choice(_common_symbols)
    elif strat == "prefixed":
        base = rng.choice(_common_prefixes) + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 24)
    elif strat == "namespaced":
        base = _namespace(rng) + rng.choice(_common_prefixes).rstrip("_") + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 20)
    elif strat == "compound":
        base = rng.choice(_common_prefixes) + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 20) + _version_tag(rng)
    elif strat == "mangled_like":
        base = rng.choice(_common_prefixes) + _rand_ident(rng, 3, 16)
        base += rng.choice([".", "_"]) + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 6)
    elif strat == "bare_ident":
        base = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 20)
    elif strat == "edge_short":
        base = rng.choice(["g", "_", "x", "ggml", "gg"])  # minimal but valid
    elif strat == "edge_long":
        # ensure length under _MAX_LEN when suffix added
        core = _rand_ident(rng, 60, 120)
        base = rng.choice(_common_prefixes) + core
    elif strat == "camel_case":
        parts = [rng.choice(["Get", "Set", "Init", "Free", "Graph", "Backend", "Buffer", "Tensor"]) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]
        base = rng.choice(["ggml", "gguf", "GGML"]).lower() + "_" + "".join(parts)
    else:
        base = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 24)

    # Occasionally append numeric suffixes
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base += rng.choice(["_1", "_2", "_3", "32", "64", "_fp16", "_fp32"]) 

    # Occasionally append linker-style suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        base += rng.choice(_suffixes)

    # Bound length
    if len(base) > _MAX_LEN:
        base = base[:_MAX_LEN]
    return base


def _edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty string
        "\t",  # control but non-NUL
        "ggml",  # plain library root
        "ggml_backend",  # partial prefix
        "ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address",  # self query
        "GGML_BACKEND_REG_GET_PROC_ADDRESS",  # case variant
        "_ggml_internal",  # leading underscore
        "ggml_backend_cuda_init@v2",  # versioned
        "ggml-backend.cuda",  # dash and dot
        "ggml::backend::cuda_init",  # C++-style namespace
        "ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type@@LIBGGML_1",  # double-@ version
    ]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose between edge cases and constructed symbols
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        sym = rng.choice(_edge_cases(rng))
    else:
        sym = _build_symbol(rng)

    # Ensure it's ASCII-only printable where possible; replace any accidental non-printable with underscore
    cleaned = []
    for ch in sym:
        o = ord(ch)
        if 32 <= o <= 126:  # printable ASCII
            cleaned.append(ch)
        else:
            cleaned.append("_")
    sym = "".join(cleaned)

    # Final clamp and encode. We avoid embedding NUL so that the C++ fuzzer uses std::string::c_str() safely.
    if len(sym) > _MAX_LEN:
        sym = sym[:_MAX_LEN]

    return sym.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

import io
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

def _rand_str(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=32) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # GGUF strings are UTF-8; use simple printable ASCII and some unicode
    alphabet = [*(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-:/."),]
    s = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s

# GGUF constants
GGUF_MAGIC = b"GGUF"
GGUF_VERSION = 3  # widely supported

# GGUF type ids
GGUF_TYPE_UINT8   = 0
GGUF_TYPE_INT8    = 1
GGUF_TYPE_UINT16  = 2
GGUF_TYPE_INT16   = 3
GGUF_TYPE_UINT32  = 4
GGUF_TYPE_INT32   = 5
GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32 = 6
GGUF_TYPE_BOOL    = 7
GGUF_TYPE_STRING  = 8
GGUF_TYPE_ARRAY   = 9
GGUF_TYPE_UINT64  = 10
GGUF_TYPE_INT64   = 11
GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64 = 12

# Utility write helpers

def _p64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<Q', x)

def _p32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x)

def _p16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x)

def _p8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<B', x)


def _write_string(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # GGUF string: u64 length, then raw bytes
    return _p64(len(s)) + s


def _write_kv(rng: random.Random, key: bytes, vtype: int, value_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += _write_string(key)
    out += _p32(vtype)
    out += value_bytes
    return bytes(out)


def _enc_value(rng: random.Random, vtype: int):
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_UINT8:
        return _p8(rng.randrange(0, 256))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_INT8:
        return struct.pack('<b', rng.randrange(-128, 128))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_UINT16:
        return _p16(rng.randrange(0, 65536))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_INT16:
        return struct.pack('<h', rng.randrange(-32768, 32768))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_UINT32:
        return _p32(rng.getrandbits(32))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_INT32:
        return struct.pack('<i', rng.randrange(-2**31, 2**31-1))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32:
        # generate some interesting floats
        choices = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 3.14159, float('inf'), float('-inf')]
        v = rng.choice(choices + [rng.uniform(-1e5, 1e5)])
        # replace NaN with 0 to keep validity predictable
        if isinstance(v, float) and (v != v):
            v = 0.0
        return struct.pack('<f', v)
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_BOOL:
        return _p8(rng.randrange(0, 2))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_STRING:
        s = _rand_str(rng, 0, 40)
        return _write_string(s)
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_UINT64:
        return _p64(rng.getrandbits(64))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_INT64:
        return struct.pack('<q', rng.randrange(-2**63, 2**63-1))
    if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64:
        v = rng.uniform(-1e10, 1e10)
        return struct.pack('<d', v)
    raise ValueError('unsupported vtype')


def _make_metadata(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a small but valid set of metadata keys commonly seen by loaders
    # Many loaders expect or handle these standard keys; include a mix
    kv = bytearray()

    # architecture string
    arch = rng.choice([b"llama", b"falcon", b"mpt", b"mamba", b"gptj", b"qwen"])
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"general.architecture", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _write_string(arch))

    # name and description
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"general.name", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _write_string(_rand_str(rng, 3, 16)))
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"general.description", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _write_string(_rand_str(rng, 0, 64)))

    # context length and vocab size
    n_ctx = rng.choice([128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096])
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"llm.context_length", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _p32(n_ctx))
    vocab = rng.choice([256, 32000, 50257, 65536])
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"tokenizer.ggml.tokens", GGUF_TYPE_ARRAY, _enc_string_array(rng, vocab_small=True))

    # Some booleans and numerical params
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"general.quantized", GGUF_TYPE_BOOL, _p8(rng.randrange(0, 2)))
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"llm.embedding_length", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _p32(rng.choice([128, 256, 512, 1024])))

    # Optional rope params
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"llm.rope.freq_base", GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32, struct.pack('<f', rng.choice([10000.0, 5000.0, 1000.0])))
    kv += _write_kv(rng, b"llm.rope.freq_scale", GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32, struct.pack('<f', rng.choice([1.0, 0.5, 2.0])))

    # Add a couple of random keys of mixed types to increase coverage
    extra_keys = rng.randint(2, 6)
    type_choices = [GGUF_TYPE_UINT8, GGUF_TYPE_INT8, GGUF_TYPE_UINT16, GGUF_TYPE_INT16,
                    GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, GGUF_TYPE_INT32, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32, GGUF_TYPE_BOOL,
                    GGUF_TYPE_STRING, GGUF_TYPE_UINT64, GGUF_TYPE_INT64, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64]
    for i in range(extra_keys):
        key = b"extra.key." + str(i).encode()
        t = rng.choice(type_choices)
        kv += _write_kv(rng, key, t, _enc_value(rng, t))

    return bytes(kv)


def _enc_string_array(rng: random.Random, vocab_small=False) -> bytes:
    # GGUF array encoding:
    # u32 element_type, u64 array_length, then elements encoded per type
    # For strings: each element is encoded as GGUF string (u64 len + bytes)
    out = bytearray()
    out += _p32(GGUF_TYPE_STRING)
    if vocab_small:
        # keep small to stay under 4096 bytes
        n = rng.randint(8, 64)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(1, 16)
    out += _p64(n)
    for _ in range(n):
        token = _rand_str(rng, 1, 8)
        out += _write_string(token)
    return bytes(out)


def _build_tensor_info(rng: random.Random, name: bytes, ne: Tuple[int, ...], ttype: int, offset: int) -> bytes:
    # Per tensor header entry:
    # name (gguf string)
    # type (u32 ggml_type)
    # n_dims (u32)
    # dims: for i in n_dims -> u64
    # offset (u64) from tensor data section start
    b = bytearray()
    b += _write_string(name)
    b += _p32(ttype)
    b += _p32(len(ne))
    for d in ne:
        b += _p64(d)
    b += _p64(offset)
    return bytes(b)


def _ggml_type_from_choice(choice: int) -> int:
    # Map a subset of ggml types that are common and easy to pack raw as fp32/f16/iq, but we will emit F32 data for simplicity.
    # In GGUF, tensor data is raw bytes; loaders use type to interpret block sizes. To keep validity, use F32 or F16 types only.
    # ggml enum: F32 = 0, F16 = 1
    return 0 if choice == 0 else 1


def _tensor_bytes_size(ttype: int, ne: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    # Only supporting F32 and F16 here to keep generation consistent
    numel = 1
    for d in ne:
        numel *= max(1, d)
    if ttype == 0:  # F32
        return numel * 4
    elif ttype == 1:  # F16
        return numel * 2
    else:
        # fallback, shouldn't occur
        return numel * 4


def _emit_tensor_data(rng: random.Random, ttype: int, ne: Tuple[int, ...]) -> bytes:
    nbytes = _tensor_bytes_size(ttype, ne)
    # Fill with reasonable numeric patterns
    buf = bytearray(nbytes)
    if ttype == 0:  # F32
        # write floats
        for i in range(0, nbytes, 4):
            v = rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)
            struct.pack_into('<f', buf, i, v)
    else:  # F16 appox by storing trunc of f32 then cast to half via rounding to 16-bit using IEEE 754 binary16 conversion approximation
        # Python stdlib lacks half pack pre-3.11; approximate using numpy is not allowed.
        # We will quantize by storing as int16 placeholder pattern; loaders will still read bytes.
        # Use a simple pattern to keep values small.
        for i in range(0, nbytes, 2):
            # store as 0 pattern or small varying pattern
            val = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
            struct.pack_into('<H', buf, i, val)
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Header
    out = bytearray()
    out += GGUF_MAGIC
    out += _p32(GGUF_VERSION)

    # We'll build a small, valid file with a handful of metadata and 1-3 tensors
    # Placeholder counts; we will fill after building sections
    # n_kv (u64), n_tensors (u64)
    kv_section = _make_metadata(rng)

    # For tensors, create names, dims, types and compute offsets into data section
    n_tensors = rng.randint(1, 3)
    tensor_infos: List[bytes] = []
    tensor_datas: List[bytes] = []

    cur_off = 0
    for i in range(n_tensors):
        name = b"tensor." + str(i).encode()
        # Choose dims up to 2D with small sizes to keep file small
        nd = rng.choice([1, 2])
        if nd == 1:
            ne = (rng.choice([8, 16, 32, 64, 128]),)
        else:
            ne = (rng.choice([4, 8, 16, 32]), rng.choice([4, 8, 16, 32]))
        ttype = _ggml_type_from_choice(rng.randrange(0, 2))
        tbytes = _tensor_bytes_size(ttype, ne)
        tensor_infos.append(_build_tensor_info(rng, name, ne, ttype, cur_off))
        tensor_datas.append(_emit_tensor_data(rng, ttype, ne))
        cur_off += tbytes

    # Now assemble the file per GGUF v3 layout:
    # magic(4), version(u32), n_kv(u64), n_tensors(u64), kv_data..., tensor_infos..., tensor_data...
    out += _p64(_count_kv_entries(kv_section))  # number of kv entries
    out += _p64(n_tensors)

    # Append kv section as-is (already encoded key+type+value tuples). The count above must match entries.
    out += kv_section

    # Append tensor infos
    for inf in tensor_infos:
        out += inf

    # Append tensor data
    for td in tensor_datas:
        out += td

    # Ensure the file is not bigger than 4096 bytes; if too large, trim by reducing tokens next time via seed variance
    return bytes(out[:4096])


def _count_kv_entries(kv_bytes: bytes) -> int:
    # Walk encoded kv_bytes to count entries: format is [str][u32 type][value]
    # Since we constructed it locally, we can count by decoding iteratively.
    # This is only used to derive count for header.
    cnt = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(kv_bytes)
    while i < n:
        if i + 8 > n:
            break
        l = struct.unpack_from('<Q', kv_bytes, i)[0]
        i += 8 + l  # name
        if i + 4 > n:
            break
        vtype = struct.unpack_from('<I', kv_bytes, i)[0]
        i += 4
        # advance value
        if vtype == GGUF_TYPE_STRING:
            if i + 8 > n: break
            sl = struct.unpack_from('<Q', kv_bytes, i)[0]
            i += 8 + sl
        elif vtype == GGUF_TYPE_ARRAY:
            if i + 12 > n: break
            etype = struct.unpack_from('<I', kv_bytes, i)[0]
            i += 4
            alen = struct.unpack_from('<Q', kv_bytes, i)[0]
            i += 8
            if etype == GGUF_TYPE_STRING:
                for _ in range(alen):
                    if i + 8 > n: break
                    sl = struct.unpack_from('<Q', kv_bytes, i)[0]
                    i += 8 + sl
            else:
                # sizes for scalar types
                sz = {GGUF_TYPE_UINT8:1, GGUF_TYPE_INT8:1, GGUF_TYPE_UINT16:2, GGUF_TYPE_INT16:2,
                      GGUF_TYPE_UINT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_INT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_BOOL:1,
                      GGUF_TYPE_UINT64:8, GGUF_TYPE_INT64:8, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64:8}.get(etype, 1)
                i += alen * sz
        else:
            sz = {GGUF_TYPE_UINT8:1, GGUF_TYPE_INT8:1, GGUF_TYPE_UINT16:2, GGUF_TYPE_INT16:2,
                  GGUF_TYPE_UINT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_INT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32:4, GGUF_TYPE_BOOL:1,
                  GGUF_TYPE_UINT64:8, GGUF_TYPE_INT64:8, GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64:8}.get(vtype, 1)
            i += sz
        cnt += 1
    return cnt
